record.original_question: For an even integer m, which non-bipartite graph with m edges, containing neither C_3 nor C_5 as a subgraph, has the maximum spectral radius?

evidence.quote: Problem 4 (Sun and Li [39], 2023). For even m, what is the extremal graph among all {C3, C5}-free non-bipartite graphs with m edges, achieving the maximum spectral radius?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $G$ be a simple graph and let $\rho(G)$ denote its spectral radius, i.e., the largest eigenvalue of its adjacency matrix. A graph is said to be $\{C_3,C_5\}$-free if it contains neither a triangle nor a $5$-cycle as a (not necessarily induced) subgraph, and it is non-bipartite if it contains at least one odd cycle. For an even positive integer $m$, determine the graph(s) attaining the maximum value of $\rho(G)$ among all $\{C_3,C_5\}$-free non-bipartite graphs $G$ with exactly $m$ edges, and compute this maximum spectral radius.
artifact.category_tag: spectral graph theory / extremal spectral radius
artifact.status_search_result: The problem was posed by Sun and Li (2023) in their work on the maximum spectral radius of $\{C_3,C_5\}$-free graphs of given size, where the extremal graph is identified only for odd $m$. Recent 2024–2025 surveys and follow-up works on related Brualdi–Hoffman–Turán type problems still list the even-$m$ non-bipartite case as an open question, with no published full characterization located.

status_evidence.title: The maximum spectral radius of {C3,C5}-free graphs of given size
status_evidence.snippet: Sun and Li (2023) determine the maximum spectral radius of {C3,C5}-free graphs of given size; the characterization of the extremal graph is given only when m is odd.
status_evidence.claim: Original source of the problem; even-m non-bipartite case left open.

status_evidence.title: Spectral extremal problems for non-bipartite graphs without odd cycles
status_evidence.snippet: Recent 2025 work addressing spectral extremal problems for non-bipartite graphs forbidding odd cycles, citing the {C3,C5}-free even-size question as motivation.
status_evidence.claim: Recent activity but no resolution of the even-m {C3,C5}-free non-bipartite case found.
